Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

An internal combustion engine comprises an exhaust purification catalyst and an air-fuel ratio sensor arranged at a downstream side of the exhaust purification catalyst, stops or decreases a feed of fuel as fuel cut control, and controls an air-fuel ratio of exhaust gas to a rich air-fuel ratio after the end of the fuel cut control as post reset rich control. The diagnosis system calculates a first characteristic of change of air-fuel ratio at the time when the output air-fuel ratio first passes a first air-fuel ratio region leaner than a stoichiometric air-fuel ratio and a second characteristic of change of air-fuel ratio at the time when the output air-fuel ratio first passes a second air-fuel ratio region including a stoichiometric air-fuel ratio. The diagnosis system diagnoses the abnormality of the air-fuel ratio sensor based on the first characteristic of change of air-fuel ratio and the second characteristic of change of air-fuel ratio. As a result, it is possible to suppress the effects of the change of state of the exhaust purification catalyst while accurately diagnosing the abnormality of deterioration of response of a downstream side air-fuel ratio sensor.

An internal combustion engine is equipped with an exhaust purification catalyst and an air-fuel ratio sensor positioned downstream of that catalyst. As part of fuel cut control, the engine stops or reduces fuel supply, and after this fuel cut control ends, it performs post-reset rich control by regulating the exhaust gas air-fuel ratio to a rich air-fuel ratio.

The diagnosis system determines a first air-fuel-ratio change characteristic when the detected output air-fuel ratio first enters a first air-fuel ratio range that is leaner than the stoichiometric air-fuel ratio. It also determines a second air-fuel-ratio change characteristic when the detected output air-fuel ratio first enters a second air-fuel ratio range that includes the stoichiometric air-fuel ratio.

Using both the first and second air-fuel-ratio change characteristics, the diagnosis system identifies abnormalities in the air-fuel ratio sensor. This makes it possible to reduce the influence of changes in the condition of the exhaust purification catalyst while still accurately detecting deterioration in the response of the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor.

The internal combustion engine is equipped with an exhaust purification catalyst provided in an exhaust passage, and an air-fuel ratio sensor arranged downstream of the catalyst. The downstream air-fuel ratio sensor detects the air-fuel ratio of exhaust gas after it has passed through the catalyst, and its output is used for monitoring the exhaust purification performance and for diagnosing the condition of the sensor itself.

The engine control system performs fuel cut control under predetermined operating conditions. During fuel cut control, the supply of fuel to the engine is stopped or reduced, for example during deceleration. When the fuel cut control ends and fuel injection is resumed, the system carries out post reset rich control. In this control, the air-fuel ratio is temporarily made richer than the stoichiometric air-fuel ratio in order to restore or adjust the oxygen storage state of the exhaust purification catalyst.

The diagnosis system monitors the output of the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor during this period after the end of fuel cut control. First, when the output of the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor initially passes through a lean region, the system calculates a first air-fuel ratio change characteristic. This characteristic represents the response behavior of the sensor while the detected air-fuel ratio is in the lean range.

Next, when the output of the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor initially passes through a region that includes the stoichiometric air-fuel ratio, the diagnosis system calculates a second air-fuel ratio change characteristic. This second characteristic represents the response behavior of the sensor around the stoichiometric point, where the air-fuel ratio changes from lean toward rich as a result of the post reset rich control.

By using both the first air-fuel ratio change characteristic and the second air-fuel ratio change characteristic, the system can diagnose deterioration in the response of the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor. In particular, the diagnosis is performed in a manner that suppresses or reduces the influence of changes in the state of the exhaust purification catalyst, such as variations in its oxygen storage amount caused by the preceding fuel cut operation. As a result, the system can more accurately determine whether the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor has degraded, while avoiding erroneous diagnosis caused by temporary changes in catalyst condition.
outputs.L4:
A diagnosis system for an internal combustion engine is configured to determine whether a downstream air-fuel ratio sensor has suffered response deterioration. The internal combustion engine includes an exhaust passage, an exhaust purification catalyst provided in the exhaust passage, and a downstream air-fuel ratio sensor disposed downstream of the exhaust purification catalyst. The downstream air-fuel ratio sensor detects an air-fuel ratio of exhaust gas after the exhaust gas has passed through the catalyst, and its output is used for engine control and catalyst monitoring.

In this system, diagnosis is performed under a controlled operating condition in order to reduce variation caused by normal engine operation. First, fuel cut control is executed. During fuel cut control, fuel injection to the engine is temporarily stopped, so that a lean exhaust gas atmosphere containing excess oxygen is supplied to the exhaust purification catalyst. As a result, oxygen is stored in the catalyst, and the output of the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor shifts toward a lean-side value.

After the fuel cut control is ended and fuel injection is resumed, post-reset rich control is performed. In the post-reset rich control, the air-fuel ratio of the mixture supplied to the engine is made richer than the stoichiometric air-fuel ratio for a predetermined period or until a predetermined condition is satisfied. This rich exhaust gas consumes oxygen stored in the exhaust purification catalyst and causes the air-fuel ratio downstream of the catalyst to change from a lean state toward a rich state.

The diagnosis system monitors the output of the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor during this transition. In particular, the system evaluates sensor response by using two air-fuel ratio change characteristics obtained as the sensor output first passes through a lean-side region and then through a region related to the stoichiometric air-fuel ratio. These characteristics may include, for example, a rate of change of the sensor output, a time required for the output to pass between predetermined air-fuel ratio thresholds, an integrated amount of output change, or another parameter representing the dynamic response of the sensor.

By using two different change characteristics instead of relying on a single output threshold or a single delay time, the system can distinguish deterioration of the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor from changes in the state of the exhaust purification catalyst. The condition of the catalyst, such as its oxygen storage amount, temperature, or purification performance, can vary from one operating condition to another and can influence the timing and shape of the downstream air-fuel ratio transition. However, evaluating the sensor response at multiple stages of the transition makes it possible to suppress the influence of such catalyst variations.

The diagnosis system therefore determines that the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor has deteriorated when the detected air-fuel ratio change characteristics indicate that the sensor output changes more slowly than expected or otherwise deviates from a normal response pattern. Conversely, when the two characteristics correspond to a normal response, the system determines that the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor is functioning properly.

Through this procedure, accurate detection of response deterioration of the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor can be achieved. Since the diagnosis is performed after fuel cut control and during post-reset rich control, and since the evaluation is based on the behavior of the sensor output as it passes through lean and stoichiometric-related regions, the diagnosis is less susceptible to fluctuations in the exhaust purification catalyst condition. As a result, false determinations are reduced, and the reliability of downstream air-fuel ratio sensor diagnosis is improved.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” may be one of the smallest words in the English language, but it is also one of the most important. As a definite article, “the” helps us refer to specific people, places, objects, or ideas. Instead of saying “a book,” which could mean any book, we say “the book” when both the speaker and listener know exactly which book is being discussed.

This simple word adds clarity and precision to communication. For example, “I visited the museum” suggests a particular museum, while “I visited a museum” is more general. In this way, “the” helps shape meaning and gives sentences a stronger sense of direction.

“The” is used everywhere: in conversation, writing, headlines, titles, and everyday instructions. It appears in phrases like “the world,” “the future,” “the best,” and “the beginning.” Although it often goes unnoticed, it plays a key role in making English sound natural and complete.

In many ways, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have a big impact. Without it, English would be less clear, less specific, and much harder to understand.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a diagnosis system that detects deterioration in the response of an air-fuel ratio sensor downstream of an exhaust purification catalyst after fuel cut control in an internal combustion engine.
counterfactuals.output: A diagnosis system for an internal combustion engine includes an exhaust purification catalyst disposed in an exhaust passage, an air-fuel ratio sensor disposed downstream of the catalyst, and a control unit configured to execute fuel cut control during engine operation. After termination of the fuel cut control and resumption of fuel supply, the control unit monitors an output of the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor during a period in which an exhaust air-fuel ratio downstream of the catalyst changes from a lean state caused by the fuel cut control toward a richer state. The control unit determines a response characteristic of the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor based on a change in the sensor output, such as a response delay time, an output change rate, or a time required for the output to cross a predetermined threshold. When the determined response characteristic indicates that the sensor output changes more slowly than a prescribed criterion, the control unit diagnoses deterioration in the response of the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor. Accordingly, response deterioration of the air-fuel ratio sensor can be accurately detected using exhaust gas behavior following fuel cut control.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the following invention in one paragraph using formal patent language: an engine performs fuel cut, then rich control, monitors downstream air-fuel ratio changes through lean and stoichiometric regions, and diagnoses sensor abnormality while reducing catalyst-state influence.
counterfactuals.output: An apparatus and method for diagnosing an abnormality of an air-fuel ratio sensor are provided, wherein an internal combustion engine is controlled to execute a fuel-cut operation and, after termination of the fuel-cut operation, to perform rich air-fuel ratio control. During a transition of exhaust gas composition caused by the rich control, an output of a downstream air-fuel ratio sensor disposed downstream of an exhaust purification catalyst is monitored as the detected air-fuel ratio changes from a lean region through a stoichiometric region toward a rich region. A diagnostic determination of sensor abnormality is made based on characteristics of the sensor output during said transition, such as response behavior or timing relative to predetermined air-fuel ratio regions. By conducting the diagnosis after fuel cut and during the controlled rich transition, the influence of the oxygen storage state or other catalyst conditions on the downstream sensor output is reduced, thereby improving the accuracy and reliability of detecting deterioration, delay, or other abnormal behavior of the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an abstract for an automotive exhaust sensor diagnostic method involving a catalyst, a downstream air-fuel ratio sensor, fuel cut control, post-reset rich control, and comparison of first and second air-fuel ratio change characteristics.
counterfactuals.output: An automotive exhaust sensor diagnostic method is provided for determining a response condition of an air-fuel ratio sensor disposed downstream of an exhaust purification catalyst. The method includes executing fuel cut control during operation of an internal combustion engine to introduce oxygen into an exhaust passage and thereby change an oxygen storage state of the catalyst. After termination of the fuel cut control and reset of an accumulated air amount or oxygen storage related parameter, post-reset rich control is performed to supply a rich air-fuel mixture to the engine. During the post-reset rich control, an output of the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor is monitored, and a first air-fuel ratio change characteristic is obtained based on a change in the sensor output occurring before or during a transition of the catalyst from an oxygen-storing state toward a reduced state. A second air-fuel ratio change characteristic is also obtained based on a subsequent change in the downstream sensor output after the rich exhaust gas has passed through the catalyst. The diagnostic method compares the first and second air-fuel ratio change characteristics, such as response timing, change amount, slope, or integrated output behavior, and determines whether the downstream air-fuel ratio sensor has degraded or is abnormal based on the comparison result. This enables accurate diagnosis of sensor responsiveness while reducing influence from catalyst oxygen storage capacity and operating condition variations.
